generator.pairing: Same (x1, x2, noise_z) and split assignment reused across A/B/C for paired regime comparison.

split.policy: 60/20/20 train/validation/test on base row_id; identical labels for all regimes

pre_registered_pilot_protocol.primary_metric: Test negative log-likelihood (NLL) under Normal predictive distribution
secondary_metrics: RMSE of location parameter vs y
diagnostic_analyses: Correlation or rank correlation between predicted scale/width and true_sigma
Binned by abs(x1) quantiles: mean predicted width vs mean true_sigma

hypotheses.H1_regime_A: Under regime A, natural and ordinary multiparameter NGBoost achieve lower test NLL than homoscedastic NormalFixedVar because sigma(x) varies with abs(x1).
hypotheses.H2_width_monotonicity_A: Under regime A, predicted interval width increases with abs(x1) in the same direction as true_sigma (binned analysis).
hypotheses.H3_regime_B_control: Under regime B (constant sigma), homoscedastic model is not required to lose decisively; regime B is a calibration control not a victory condition for natural gradient.
hypotheses.H4_regime_C: Under regime C (doubled heteroscedastic), input-dependent models should still track widening sigma; magnitude differs from A by design.

non_requirements: Natural gradient need not win every regime.
Regime B is explicitly a homoscedastic control.
pre_registered_pilot_protocol.model_seed_note: Data frozen with seeds 0/1; model loops use seed 1 per proposal evidence unless a separate handoff changes this.

scientific_framing: Constructed evidence probing NGBoost input-dependent uncertainty: known mu(x) and sigma(x) with paired regimes isolate heteroscedasticity as the controlled variable rather than arbitrary synthetic rows.
